# Tutorials

The core tutorials build one model a step at a time: a measles outbreak in a town, which gains a latent period, age groups, vaccination, repeated runs, data to fit it to, and other towns. Each takes about ten minutes, starts with the model so far (so you can start at any one), and ends with exercises.

## Core tutorials

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-6}
[**T1: Getting started**](tutorials/t1_intro.qmd)

A measles outbreak as an SIR model: run it, plot it, and check what Starsim built.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T2: Building your model**](tutorials/t2_model.qmd)

The first model again, in more depth: what each part means, results, time, and parameters.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T3: Disease structure**](tutorials/t3_structure.qmd)

A latent period, durations, and branching, and how to see a model's diagram and equations.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T4: Age groups and contacts**](tutorials/t4_ages.qmd)

Who mixes with whom: age groups, contact matrices, and real populations.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T5: Vaccination and scenarios**](tutorials/t5_vaccination.qmd)

Vaccines and other interventions, and comparing scenarios side by side.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T6: Repeated runs and uncertainty**](tutorials/t6_uncertainty.qmd)

How much an outbreak varies by chance, and how to show it.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T7: Calibration**](tutorials/t7_calibration.qmd)

Fitting the model's parameters to reported cases, and projecting from the fit.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T8: Places and movement**](tutorials/t8_places.qmd)

Several towns, and how an outbreak travels between them.
:::
:::

## Going further

These tutorials go deeper into topics that some models need and others don't. They can be read in any order after the core tutorials. Two suggested routes:

- **Modeling individuals, networks, or behavior:** G1, G2, G5, and G6.
- **Coming from compartmental (ODE) models:** G3, G4, G7, and G5.

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-6}
[**G1: Networks**](tutorials/g1_networks.qmd)

Contact networks between people, and when a model needs one.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**G2: Demographics**](tutorials/g2_demographics.qmd)

Births, deaths, and pregnancy, from a country's data.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**G3: Stratification in depth**](tutorials/g3_strata.qmd)

Several dimensions at once, and people moving between groups.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**G4: Parameters over time**](tutorials/g4_time.qmd)

Values that change over time: time series, seasons, and school terms.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**G5: Several diseases**](tutorials/g5_diseases.qmd)

Diseases that interact, and how to link them.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**G6: Modules written as code**](tutorials/g6_code.qmd)

Writing your own behavior in Python, next to a declared model.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**G7: Bringing a model in**](tutorials/g7_import.qmd)

Importing a model from another framework, and comparing models.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**G8: When the model doesn't fit**](tutorials/g8_extending.qmd)

A classic model with features Starsim has no words for, in four steps from declared to compiled code.
:::
:::

The answers to the exercises are in the [solutions](tutorials/solutions.qmd).

:::{.callout-note}
You can download these tutorials as Jupyter notebooks to run them locally. Look for the download button at the top of each tutorial.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Running tutorials locally

To run these tutorials locally:

1. Clone the Starsim repository
2. Install Starsim and its dependencies
3. Navigate to the `docs/tutorials` directory
4. Convert to Jupyter: `./convert_notebooks` (or just open them directly if `jupytext` is installed)
5. Launch Jupyter: `jupyter lab`
:::
